formulas.formula: Budget, pay off debt and grow your savings, all in one place. Everything is linked.
Fills in from the year above (this year if blank).
To change it, select the money cells and use Format > Number.
1. In YOUR SETUP, type your budget year. Every tab follows it.
2. Open Budget Plan. Rename the categories to fit your life and type a Monthly Amount for each.
3. Log every paycheck and purchase on Transactions: date, category (pick from the list) and amount.
4. The Dashboard shows your whole year; the Monthly Dashboard shows any month you pick.
5. DEBT: list your debts on Debt Payoff (balance and interest rate) and plan a payment for each on Budget Plan.
6. Then open Payoff Plan: pick Snowball or Avalanche, add an extra amount, and see your debt-free date.
7. SAVINGS: set long-term goals on Savings Goals and dated costs (trips, gifts) on Sinking Funds.
8. For a fun boost, start the 52-week Savings Challenge and tick a box every week.
9. Once a month, update Debt Payoff (current balance), Savings Goals and Net Worth.
10. Got a refund? Log it as a negative amount in the same category.
11. The example numbers show a whole year. To start fresh, go to Transactions, select columns A to F
from row 2 down and press Delete (don't delete the rows). Then type over the other examples.
Your whole year at a glance: totals, savings rate, charts, top categories, net worth.
Pick a month at the top: its own cards, budget vs. actual and top spending.
Your categories and how much you plan for each one, every month of the year.
One list for every paycheck and purchase. Everything else reads from here.
Every category, every month, side by side, with totals and monthly averages.
A checklist of your bills with due days. Tick a box when a bill is paid.
Everything you pay for regularly, what it costs per year, and what to cancel.
Your debts, how much you paid down this year, interest paid and months left.
Snowball or avalanche: payoff order, debt-free date, interest saved, month by month.
Long-term goals with progress bars, fed by your savings transactions.
Money set aside for a dated cost: how much a month you need, and if your plan covers it.
The 52-week challenge: tick a box each week and watch the total grow.
What you own minus what you owe, month by month, with a chart.
White cells: type your numbers here.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you. No typing needed.
Red: something to check (over budget, a missing category, text in a number cell).
Green: on track, paid or better than planned.
Pay yourself first: move money to savings on payday, before you spend.
Build a small emergency fund (even $1,000) before throwing everything at debt.
Snowball keeps you motivated with quick wins. Avalanche saves the most interest. Both work: pick one.
Every raise, refund or side-hustle dollar can go to the Payoff Plan's extra amount.
Check the Dashboard at the end of each month and adjust next month's plan.
Buy with a credit card? Log each purchase in its category. Under Debt, log only what you pay toward an old balance, so nothing counts twice.
Thank you for your purchase! Here's to less debt and more savings.
Everything here updates from your Transactions tab.
Tip: if something looks off, check 'Transactions to fix' above and the Check column on Transactions.
Pick a month. Everything below follows it. It all comes from Transactions.
Pick from the list, or type 3 letters like Sep.
Spending vs. last month: + means you spent less than the month before.
=IF(INDEX('Year Summary'!$D$67:$O$67,1,$Q$3)=0,"No transactions logged for this month yet.",INDEX('Year Summary'!$D$67:$O$67,1,$Q$3)&" transactions logged this month.")
Type a Monthly Amount and it fills every month. Different in one month? Type over that month (it turns blue). Rename categories, but don't insert or delete rows.
Red category name: it's listed twice, has amounts but no name, or uses * ? ~ or starts with < > = (rename it).
Left to Plan: green = every dollar has a job, yellow = money not planned yet, red = planned more than you earn.

=IF(AND(A{row}="",B{row}="",D{row}=""),"",IF(OR(NOT(ISNUMBER(A{row})),N(A{row})<1,N(A{row})>2958465),"Check the date",IF(YEAR(A{row})<>'Start Here'!$D$8,"Not in "&'Start Here'!$D$8,IF(B{row}="","Pick a category",IF(G{row}="Not found","Category not on Budget Plan",IF(D{row}="","Add an amount",IF(NOT(ISNUMBER(D{row})),"Amount must be a number","OK")))))))
Filled in automatically from Transactions. Nothing to type here. Budget So Far = your plan for the months that have transactions.
Total of the bills on this list
Tick the box under the month when a bill is paid. Paid boxes turn green.
Bills on autopay still need a check: make sure the money is there before the due day.
Log the payment on Transactions too, so it counts in your budget.
Cancel the ones marked Cancel and you save per year:
Billing: pick Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly or Yearly. Monthly and Yearly Cost fill in.
Renews On: the next date you'll be charged. Set a reminder a few days before.
Budget the monthly total under Subscriptions on Budget Plan, and log each charge on Transactions.
Pick a debt from your Debt categories, then type the balance on January 1, the interest rate (22.99 or 22.99%) and, once a month, the Current Balance from your statement.
Paid This Year fills in from Transactions. Interest & Charges = what you paid minus how much the balance went down (interest, fees and any new purchases). Keep Current Balance up to date.
Monthly Payment comes from Budget Plan. Months Left assumes you keep paying that amount.
Snowball: pay extra on Payoff Order 1 (the smallest balance) first. When it's gone, roll its payment into the next one.
'Payment too low' means the payment doesn't cover the monthly interest yet. A rate under 1%? Type it with the % sign, like 0.9%.

formula: OR($K2="Payment too low",$K2="Add it to Budget Plan",$K2="Fix a payment")

section_bars.label: MONTH-BY-MONTH PLAN (BALANCE LEFT AFTER EACH MONTH'S PAYMENTS)

formulas.formula: Your debt-free plan. Balances and rates come from Debt Payoff; payments from Budget Plan.
Snowball: smallest balance first (quick wins). Avalanche: highest interest first (saves the most).
On top of your planned payments. It goes to debt #1; when a debt is gone, its payment rolls on.
The month of your first plan payment. Use the month after your Current Balances.
Every month you pay each debt's planned payment, and your extra goes to debt #1.
When a debt is paid off, its payment rolls into the next one, so your monthly total stays the same.
Minimums only = the same payments with no extra and no rolling over. Switch Snowball / Avalanche to compare.
Over 30 years? A payment doesn't cover its interest: raise it on Budget Plan or add an extra amount.
Pick a goal from your Savings categories (or type your own), then add the Target and what you had saved on January 1 (Starting Balance).
Added This Year fills in from Transactions: every transfer you log to that category counts.
Monthly Plan comes from Budget Plan (the category's year total divided by 12).
Tip: build a starter emergency fund of $1,000 first, then grow it to 3-6 months of expenses.

=IF(AND(A{row}="",B{row}="",C{row}=""),"",IF(B{row}="","Pick a savings category",IF(O{row}="","Pick a savings category from the list",IF(P{row},"Category already used (above or on Savings Goals)",IF(NOT(AND(ISNUMBER(C{row}),C{row}>0)),"Add a target",IF(H{row}=0,"Funded ✓",IF(K{row}="","Add a due date",IF(K{row}<1,"Due date is before this year",IF(N(M{row})>=L{row}-0.005,"On track","Plan "&TEXT(L{row}-N(M{row}),"$#,##0.00")&" more a month")))))))))
A sinking fund is money you set aside a little at a time for a cost you know is coming: a trip, holiday gifts, car repairs, insurance, a new phone.
Name the fund, pick the Savings category you move the money into (log those transfers on Transactions), and type the Target, Due Date and what you already have.
Needed / Month = what's left to reach the target, spread from January to the end of the due month. Saved and Planned count the same months.
Give each fund its own Savings category (not one a Savings Goal uses). Need more? Rename 'Other Savings' or the blank Savings row on Budget Plan.
Tick a box each week you save. Everything else adds up for you.
Going up: week 1 saves the starting amount, week 2 twice that ... week 52 saves 52 times it.
Going down starts with week 52's amount. Same every week: save the starting amount each week.
Move the money to savings the day you tick the box.
Log it on Transactions in a Savings category too, so your budget counts it.
Missed a week? Double up next week, or just keep going. Every box counts.
Once a month, type what you own (assets) and what you owe (debts). Net worth = assets - debts.
Don't worry if it's negative at first (student loans do that). Watch the line go up.
